subject: Production: elevated 5xx/429 + timeouts — Kinetix Health (urgent)
messages:
From: Alex Jones <alex.jones@kinetix.health>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike + client timeouts

Monica,

We started seeing a big spike in 5xx and 429s hitting our Redwood-backed endpoints around 08:30 PST. Customer-facing requests are failing intermittently (mobile apps show "server error"), and our client-side metrics show aggressive retries which are likely making the situation worse.

What we see:~
- 5xx rate jumped from ~0.3% to ~7.8% between 08:30-09:10 PST
- 429s and connection timeouts occurred in bursts; retry loops on our side pushed CPU/token counts up
- Some of our DNS lookups returned SERVFAILs which matched increased latency on the first byte

We attached a short sample of errors and a link to our SLO graphs. Can you confirm if Redwood is seeing anything on your end? We need an ETA for mitigation — business impact is visible and an exec is asking for updates.

Attached: error-samples.log (500 lines, samples redacted)

--
Alex Jones
SRE Lead, Kinetix Health
alex.jones@kinetix.health

Subject: Re: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike + client timeouts

Triage notes (quick):
- Observed elevated 5xx/429 across multiple customer routes between 08:28-09:14 PST.
- Correlation: increased DNS SERVFAIL rates against dnsfast.io for our infra certificates; concurrent connection resets inside us-west-2 (AWS networking edge).
- Symptom: client retries + no jitter led to short-lived throughput saturation on a subset of inference nodes -> 503s and token timeouts.

Immediate mitigations applied:
- Scoped traffic: moved Kinetix traffic to a smaller pool with prioritized warm replicas (reduced cold-start risk).
- Applied short-term client-side advisory to reduce retry aggressiveness (Monica sent to customer).
- Enabled prefix KV cache bypass for large requests to drop heavy KV lookups that timeout under network flapping (temporary).

Next steps:
1) Contact AWS account team to confirm any regional network event (opened PD incident PD-3829).
2) Reach out to DNS provider (support@dnsfast.io) to investigate SERVFAIL spike and cached negative entries.
3) If retry storm continues, enable fallback routing policy to route to our eu model-generic pool as a temporary measure.

Attaching: pagerduty-incident-3829.txt with early logs.

—Connor
SRE (Runtime)
connor_obrien@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:22:15 -08:00
Subject: Re: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike + client timeouts — interim mitigation

Alex — quick update and temporary mitigation steps you can implement immediately:

Client-side workaround (recommended, immediate):
- Reduce retry attempts to max 2 per request with exponential backoff + full jitter.
- If possible, respect Retry-After header from 429 responses instead of immediate retry.

Redwood-side changes we pushed (temporary):
- Prioritized Kinetix traffic onto reserved warm pool to reduce timeouts.
- Enabled a strict token/req admission window for noisy clients to prevent a single client from saturating lanes.
- Prepared a fallback policy (route to eu-generic) if network flapping persists; will only enable with your signoff.

We expect visible improvement within 20–30 minutes after client-side retry reduction. Connor will monitor token error rates and I will coordinate comms.

If you want us to enable the fallback routing now, say so and we'll flip the rule (note: model latency will increase for routed requests).

—Monica

Subject: RE: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike + timeouts — AWS status

Hi Monica / team,

We observed a partial networking control-plane disruption in us-west-2 affecting a subset of customer ENIs and edge proxies between ~08:25-09:05 PST. The event caused transient connection resets and impacted DNS path stability for some providers. We engaged with our networking tier and the issue has been mitigated; normal behavior resumed at ~09:12 PST.

Actions we took:
- Cleared affected edge proxies, rotated routes for impacted hosts.
- Coordinated with the DNS provider to remove stale negative caches where encountered.
- Opening follow-up RCA; we expect an initial AWS incident summary within 48 hours.

We will continue to monitor; please share any additional logs or samples to aws-account@amazon.com and reference AWS-8842.

Regards,
AWS Account Team
aws-account@amazon.com
